entries.why_wrong: This line just declares the function and its parameter; it doesn't touch the loop's start or end bounds at all. The actual off-by-one comes from how `i` is initialized and compared inside the `for` statement, not from the function signature.

`arr[i]` is exactly how you're supposed to index into the array — the read itself isn't wrong, it just gets fed a bad range of `i` values. The real problem is upstream, where `i` starts at 1 instead of 0 and is allowed to reach `arr.length`.

This is only the closing brace that ends the loop body; it has no effect on which indices get iterated over. The skipped-first/overrun-last behavior is fully determined by the `for` header on line 1, not by where the block ends.

This brace simply closes the function definition and has no bearing on the loop's bounds. The out-of-bounds access and skipped first element trace back to the `i = 1` start and `i <= arr.length` condition, both set earlier in the loop header.
